introduction: Shaykh Aḥmad al-Aḥsá’í (d. 1826) and his successor Siyyid Káẓim Rashtí (d. 1843) founded a school within Shí‘ih Islam that read the resurrection and the return of the Imam spiritually and taught that the Promised One was near. When Siyyid Káẓim died without naming a successor his students dispersed to search; one of them, Mullá Ḥusayn, found the Báb. Bahá’u’lláh calls the two teachers “twin luminaries”. This guide gathers the references to them and to the Shaykhí school, most of whose members did not follow the Báb. The Gospel pattern is close: a forerunner, disciples sent to look, Simeon and Anna waiting, Apollos who knew only John’s baptism, and a school of the Baptist that outlived him.
questions: What did the Shaykhí teachers prepare, and how?
Siyyid Káẓim named no successor and told his students to search. What kind of leadership is that?
Why would those best prepared for a new revelation be divided by its coming?

outside.why: The Shí‘ih are content with their jurists’ rulings. Ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters.
Words from the Source about the two who prepared the way. Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.

One who had mastered the teachings of the Shaykh and the Siyyid. Apollos was mighty in the scriptures, knowing only the baptism of John, until two friends expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
After the Prophet and the Imams, the two luminaries. The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, prepare ye the way of the Lord.
A leading Shaykhí challenged. The priests and Levites asked John, who art thou?
The Shaykhís hold that conjecture in faith is not enough; certainty is required. I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by revelation.

Siyyid Káẓim sent his students to seek the Promised One. Simeon was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and it was revealed unto him that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
The Shí‘ihs had forgotten the truth of religion; the Shaykh taught spiritual meanings. The kingdom of God cometh not with observation.
People say this Cause is like Shaykh Aḥmad’s before Siyyid Káẓim. He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.
When Siyyid Káẓim was near death he spoke of what was coming. Many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them.
Moses saw the land from the mountain and did not enter it. What is the station of those who prepare a way they do not live to walk?

Statements attributed to Shaykh Aḥmad. Most Shaykhís did not become Bábís, as most of John’s followers did not at once become Christians: he must increase, but I must decrease. Why is the school of a forerunner so often the place of the strongest resistance?
